title: Validation of handgrip exercise in the echocardiographic assessment of mitral regurgitation
summary:
In this study, we aim to assess the diagnostic and prognostic value of handgrip exercise echocardiography in patients with mitral regurgitation. On the level of valve diseases, stress echocardiography is essential to unmask the significance of valve insufficiencies that appear moderate at rest by hemodynamic provocation. Bicycle exercise represents the gold standard in this respect and is recommended in defined clinical scenarios by the guidelines of the European Society of Cardiology. Likewise, isometric handgrip exercise is frequently used - here, however, there is only limited scientific evidence.
The aim is to establish a study registry in which patients are enrolled and followed up over a period of 24 months in order to determine the diagnostic and prognostic value of the handgrip examination compared to the resting examination. Within this framework, echocardiographic parameters that promote a dynamic of mitral regurgitation will be identified. Furthermore, the handgrip load will be compared with the ergonomic load. In addition, the results of the echocardiographic stress analysis will be compared to invasively measured values using exercise right heart catheterization.

interventions.name: In the study, transthoracic echocardiography is performed at rest and under handgrip exercise. This is done as part of the routine clinical examination.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- male and female patients with the diagnosis of mitral regurgitation
- age >18 years
- informed written consent
Exclusion criteria:
- no informed written consent
- age <18 years
- pregnancy
